<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
Hello <Alias=Player>,
We understand that you recently acquired, and made use of, our lantern.
Realize, the lantern is a test. It is temptation given form; a way to see if you truly have the willpower to overcome obstacles.
You do not have that willpower. In the great test of life, you did not pass. You cheated.
Now maybe you are used to an easier quality of life, one where your penance is a mere slap on the wrist.
But know that we operate differently. You do not deserve the items you acquired, you do not deserve to be Dragonborn. You do not deserve anything, because you are a failure.
And failure is punished. 

Enjoy your life,
The Cult of Sybandis

</font>

<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
By order of Justicar Elenwen, 
The following guardsmer is to be transferred to Whitehorn Pass immediately, following the crime of consorting with persons of a lesser, with intent to copulate.
All questions are to be forwarded to Justicar Numinarius, at the enclosed memospore address.

</font>

<font face='$HandwrittenFont'>
Pouring over the notes of both Sotha Sil, and Plitinius Mero's biographies, I believe I have finally discerned what this strange material is! Opening up the boundaries of Magnus' work was difficult, but it seems the liquid is not an aftereffect of ripping reality in two, but rather the result. It is the lifeblood of the world, liquid equations, but much more than that. Injecting it subjects showed an amazing increase in vitality, though often at the cost of mental sanity. More pertinent, the material, under the right circumstances, can be hardened, twisted, and most importantly, shaped. Sotha Sil's notes believe me to think that he used this material to build the so-called "Imperfect", the mechanical being to which he uploaded his imperfections.
It is evident that the material reacts to memories, which has lead me to dub it "memodermis", an appropriate name, but I can do so much more.
I have sent numerous agents down into the valleys, to open up more nodes for harvesting. Indeed, with the vast amounts of materials I have retrieved, I have been able to construct a similar giant automaton, a creation I call "Ramon". No doubt it will come in handy.

</font>

objectives.text: Find the person who sent the letter in <Alias=Location>
